claim: Schistosomes infect hundreds of millions of people in the developing world.

claim: Transmission of schistosome parasites relies on a stem cell-driven, clonal expansion of larvae inside a molluscan intermediate host.

claim: The proliferative larval cell population (germinal cells) shares some molecular signatures with stem cells from diverse organisms.

claim: There are two distinct germinal cell lineages that differ in their proliferation kinetics.

claim: A vasa/PL10 homolog is required for proliferation and maintenance of both germinal cell populations.

claim: Argonaute2 is required only for nanos-negative germinal cells.
source_text: argonaute2 and a fibroblast growth factor receptor-encoding gene are required only for nanos -negative cells

claim: A fibroblast growth factor receptor-encoding gene is required only for nanos-negative germinal cells.

claim: An ancient stem cell-based developmental program may have enabled the evolution of the complex life cycle of parasitic flatworms.
source_text: Our results suggest that an ancient stem cell-based developmental program may have enabled the evolution of the complex life cycle of parasitic flatworms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation based on the molecular similarities observed between parasitic and free-living flatworm stem cells.

claim: A population of totipotent stem cells, historically called 'germinal cells', underlies intramolluscan amplification by undergoing multiple rounds of proliferation and de novo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization.

evidence_reasoning: This is a historical model cited from previous literature (Olivier and Mao, 1949; Cort et al., 1954; Whitfield and Evans, 1983).

claim: Germinal cells were recognized by their stem cell-like morphology and rapid cycling kinetics in early ultrastructural and histological studies.
source_text: Early ultrastructural and histological studies recognized these cells by their stem cell-like morphology and rapid cycling kinetics

claim: Serial transplantation of sporocysts into naive snail hosts led to continuous sporocyst propagation and cercarial production.
source_text: serial transplantation of sporocysts into naive snail hosts led to continuous sporocyst propagation and cercarial production

claim: Division of diploid presumptive totipotent stem cells in mother sporocysts produces progeny that are able to independently initiate the embryogenesis of daughter sporocysts.

evidence_reasoning: This is a model derived from classic studies cited in the text (Whitfield and Evans, 1983).

claim: Daughter sporocysts can produce more daughter sporocysts or infective cercariae in the same manner as they were generated themselves.
source_text: These daughter sporocysts, which are essentially sacs filled with germinal cells, can then produce more daughter sporocysts or infective cercariae in the same manner as they were generated themselves.

claim: The process of multiple embryos being produced from the same zygote with no intervening gamete production represents 'polyembryony'.
source_text: This process represents 'polyembryony'—during which multiple embryos are produced from the same zygote with no intervening gamete production.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of a known biological phenomenon applied to the schistosome developmental process.

claim: A population of pluripotent stem cells called neoblasts in planarians can regenerate injured tissues and replenish a whole animal from a single cell.
source_text: In planarians, free-living flatworm relatives of schistosomes, a population of pluripotent stem cells called neoblasts can regenerate injured tissues and replenish a whole animal from a single cell
